literal_source_claim: The L^p boundedness of conjugate functions.
canonical_claim: Provisionally: for 1 < p < infinity, the periodic conjugate function (circular Hilbert transform) of an L^p function belongs to L^p and has norm at most C_p times the norm of the original function, with the operator, circle measure, scalar field, representatives, and constant fixed by the selected source.
domain_and_universes: Expected domain is the one-dimensional torus with normalized Haar measure and real- or complex-valued L^p functions; the exact circle model, scalar field, and representative convention remain open.
quantifiers: f in the source-specified L^p space
possibly a bound constant C_p depending only on p
hypotheses: integrability exponent lies strictly between 1 and infinity
f belongs to the chosen periodic L^p space
conclusion: The source-defined conjugate function exists in L^p and satisfies the source-specified L^p bound.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Endpoints p = 1 and p = infinity are not included in the strong-type claim. Mean-zero normalization, constants, almost-everywhere representatives, real versus complex scalars, and principal-value versus Fourier-multiplier definitions must be fixed rather than silently identified.
